title: config loader: layered option

facts.value: Chosen option for the config loader: option C, a layered loader. We compared three options. Option A read one JSON file and failed hard on any unknown key; it was simple but broke every user who had an old key left over. Option B merged environment variables over the file with no schema; it was flexible but a typo in a variable name silently did nothing, which cost a full afternoon in the last release. Option C, the one we chose, loads in three layers: built-in defaults, then the project file, then the user file, and checks the merged result against one schema. Unknown keys produce a warning that names the key and the layer, never an error, so old configs keep working. Each value records which layer set it, so the doctor command can print where a value came from. The schema version we agreed on for the merged result is cfg-schema-v4, and the loader must refuse any file that declares a newer schema version than that. Option C costs one extra file read at start, which we measured at under 2 ms.
Fix for 'ENOENT: no such file or directory' on first run: create the user config folder with mkdir recursive before the first write.
